display.purpose: Page-owning statements only — hero and contact. Uppercase Anton, one per screen.

headline.purpose: Section titles, paper-plate card titles, in-prose h2. Uppercase Anton.

title.purpose: Product-card titles at fixed 2rem. Uppercase Anton.

body.purpose: All long-form prose. Newsreader; italics carry taglines and asides.

label.purpose: Mono micro-labels — dates, kickers, table headers, nav, status. The connective tissue of the system.

shadows.name: tally-glow
shadows.purpose: The on-air light. Status dots representing genuinely live, currently-changing state. Never on buttons, cards, inputs, or focus rings.

shadows.name: print-offset
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on the contact title only. Two-colour registration misalignment, not a glow.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal — opacity and 28px rise over 0.7s. Decelerating, no overshoot.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions on hover/focus, 0.2s.

motion.name: grain-loop
motion.purpose: Film grain at 5.5% opacity. Incidental atmosphere; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: Ticker band. Signature element of the ink ground.

narrative.overview:
maystash reads like a technical logbook kept by someone who writes well. Evidence gets recorded plainly — dated, labelled, ruled off — and the author occasionally annotates in blue. Nothing here is decorated for the sake of decoration; the ornament is the record-keeping itself. Mono labels, dotted rules, and terse specimen cards do the structural work, and long-form prose in a real reading serif does the rest.

The palette runs near-black by default with warm bone text, and the home page interrupts itself with light paper plates — the notebook opened flat under a lamp. Klein blue is the annotation hand: selection, blockquote, title offset, the mark of the author intervening in the record. Acid green is the only thing on the site that looks powered.

Film grain sits over everything at 5.5% opacity. It is incidental atmosphere, not the thesis — it warms the black and keeps the paper plates from reading as pure digital white. Removing it would not break the system; over-emphasizing it would.
keyCharacteristics: Mono micro-labels are the dominant structural device, not an accent
Dotted and hairline rules carry hierarchy where boxes would in other systems
Flat by decree, with exactly one sanctioned exception

rules.name: The One Volt Rule
rules.body: Acid has five sanctioned roles: response (hover/focus on ink), live status (tally dots, logo cursor), emphasis (one word per page tagline), index marks (CH.05, 01), and row CTAs (WATCH, VISIT — acid at rest, and acid through the klein fill at 7.07:1). Roles 4 and 5 are paired across both reel pages. Coverage under ~5%.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: Klein is printed; acid is electric. Acid appears only in response to the reader (hover, focus) or on genuinely-changing data. Nothing is acid merely because it is important. A colour that both decorates and signals does neither job.

rules.name: The Ground Decides Rule
rules.body: Which accent carries the response is set by the ground, not by preference. On ink, acid responds (17.02:1) and Klein is unusable as a foreground (2.41:1). On paper, Klein responds (6.95:1) and acid is invisible (1.02:1). Klein-hot on ink reaches only 3.34:1 — legal for non-text marks, illegal for small text.

rules.name: The Never-Black Rule
rules.body: The ground is #0c0c0e and the foreground is #ece7dd. Pure #000 and pure #fff do not appear in this system.

rules.name: The Label Floor Rule
rules.body: No functional text renders below 11px at any viewport. Mono labels are already small by design; shrinking them further on mobile is where legibility actually breaks, not where the design gets tighter.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Anton stamps, Newsreader writes, Space Mono labels. A heading never runs in Newsreader; body copy never runs in Anton; a date never runs in anything but mono.

rules.name: The Short Shout Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to display type and mono labels. It is legitimate on headings of any length, because Anton is a display face — but a passage of running body copy never goes uppercase.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from hairlines, dotted borders, and whitespace. Reach for a border-bottom: 1px dotted before reaching for a container with a background.

rules.name: The Tally Light Rule
rules.body: The acid glow means 'this is live right now.' Applying it to anything static is a lie told in CSS. 'Building' and 'archived' are states, not signals: they take their colour flat, with no halo.

rules.name: The Flat-Everywhere-Else Rule
rules.body: Outside the tally light and the print offset, this system has no shadows. Hover states change colour and border, never elevation.

rules.name: The Sheet Rule
rules.body: Anything that spans the full viewport is a sheet and takes no corner radius. Radius signals 'this is an object you can act on.'

rules.name: The Twin Reels Rule
rules.body: /writing and /projects are the same component wearing different nouns: index mark, title, tagline, meta row, CTA. Any change to one is a change to both. They have already drifted apart once.

rules.name: The Honest Fill Rule
rules.body: A row that fills with colour on hover is promising a click. It gets that fill only when it actually has a destination — /projects gates the fill behind .is-linked, and a project with no URL stays flat.

dos: Do reach for a hairline or dotted rule before reaching for a bordered box. See The Rule-Not-Box Rule.
Do keep every functional text size at 11px or above, including mono labels on mobile.
Do use Klein for the site's own structural marks and acid strictly for reader-response and live state.
Do give full-bleed sheets zero corner radius and interactive objects a radius.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion on any new motion — the existing system disables grain, reveal, and smooth scroll completely.
Do cap prose measure (52rem wide statements, 36rem narrow) even when the container is wider.
donts: Don't add a shadow. The tally glow and the Klein print offset are the entire depth vocabulary.
Don't put the acid glow on anything whose state cannot change while the reader watches.
Don't give acid a fourth role. Response, live status, one tagline word — anything else is a violation.
Don't put Klein on ink or acid on paper as a foreground colour. See The Ground Decides Rule.
Don't set running body copy in uppercase. Headings and mono labels only.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing (cubic-bezier with an overshoot past 1). The established reveal curve is cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.6, 0.2, 1) — decelerating, no overshoot.
Don't introduce a fourth typeface. Three voices, three jobs.
Don't give a hover fill to an element with no destination. See The Honest Fill Rule.
